transcript.text: Hi, my Bosch WAN28281GB has stopped half way through a wash and is showing E18. Water still in the drum. What does that mean?

I’ve noted the E18 on the display; the step below is the right place to start either way. The most common cause is a blockage in the pump filter (also called the drain filter or trap), and it’s a free fix. On most washing machines, it’s behind a small flap or kick-plate at the bottom front. Please switch the machine off and unplug it first. If it was on a hot wash, give the water time to cool before opening anything. Put towels down and have a shallow tray or baking dish ready, as several litres of water can come out. Unscrew the filter slowly so the water comes out gradually. Don’t force it if it won’t turn. The app shows a picture and video under your reply to help you locate it. Could you check the filter and tell me what you find — was it clear, did you find and remove something, is there a blockage you can't shift, or does anything look broken?
[Helpful to see: image "Where the pump filter is" — The pump filter is usually behind a flap at the bottom front. Turn the machine off and drain any water first, then twist the filter out to clear it. Typical location — your machine may differ.; video "How to unblock the pump / drain filter" — Typical procedure for clearing a blocked pump filter and drain pump — switch the machine off and drain the water first. Access can vary by model.]
Thanks, I'll give that a go. Just to say, there's no burning smell and no water near the socket. I'll unplug it first and report back on what I find in the filter.

Thanks for letting me know. No problem if you haven’t had a chance yet. The most common cause is a blockage in the pump filter (also called the drain filter or trap), and it’s a free fix. On most washing machines, it’s behind a small flap or kick-plate at the bottom front. Please switch the machine off and unplug it first. If it was on a hot wash, give the water time to cool before opening anything. Put towels down and have a shallow tray or baking dish ready, as several litres of water can come out. Unscrew the filter slowly so the water comes out gradually. Don’t force it if it won’t turn. Could you check the filter and tell me what you find — was it clear, did you find and remove something, is there a blockage you can't shift, or does anything look broken?

Ok, I've done it now. I found a child's sock and a hair grip wrapped round the filter, plus a lot of fluff. I had to empty the water out first using the small drain hose, which took several trays. The floor got a little wet while I was draining the filter. What should I do next?

Now that the blockage is cleared, let's test it: run a drain or spin-only programme. If any water has reached the plug or socket, don't touch it — tell me straight away instead. The door will stay locked until the water has gone, so don't try to force it open. Does the water pump away now?

I've put the filter back and run a rinse & spin programme. It drains quickly now, E18 has gone and it spins normally. The water on the floor was only a little, and nothing is near the socket. Nothing has tripped either.

[Heading: Blocked pump filter]
Thanks for letting us know that the drain and spin cycle successfully emptied the water. It sounds like a blockage in the pump filter was the cause, which is now cleared. You won’t need to replace any parts. If this issue returns in the future, checking the pump filter should be your first step.
